brief.topic: Sahih al-Bukhari 935: the hour on Friday for du'a
brief.audience: Muslims who want a short, trustworthy daily reminder they can act on

coreInsight: Sahih al-Bukhari 935 mentions a short hour on Friday in which a Muslim praying and asking Allah is given what he asks, so come to Friday with your du'a ready.

hooks.text: It's Friday. Have your du'a ready.
hooks.notes: Clear on the day; the hadith pays it off.
Edges toward fear of missing out.

hooks.text: What would you ask for today?

selectionRationale: Most relevant and clearest at a glance; the teaching pays it off.

scenes.excerpt: There is an hour (opportune time) on Friday and if a Muslim gets it while praying and asks something from Allah, then Allah will definitely meet his demand

resolved.arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ، عَنْ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذَكَرَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ " فِيهِ سَاعَةٌ لاَ يُوَافِقُهَا عَبْدٌ مُسْلِمٌ، وَهْوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي، يَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى شَيْئًا إِلاَّ أَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهُ ". وَأَشَارَ بِيَدِهِ يُقَلِّلُهَا.
resolved.english: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) talked about Friday and said, "There is an hour (opportune time) on Friday and if a Muslim gets it while praying and asks something from Allah, then Allah will definitely meet his demand." And he (the Prophet) pointed out the shortness of that time with his hands
